fieldNotes.truckGate: Open campus. The large white-roof DC is set well back from E 40th Ave behind open lawn and employee parking; truck driveways run unobstructed onto the dock yard. No barrier arm, sliding/swing gate, or checkpoint pinch-point observed at any entry across multiple satellite passes and Street View headings.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No guard booth at any entrance. Modern set-back industrial-park design with no checkpoint structure.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: All dock doors run along one continuous bank on the SE long face — a single dock cluster, not physically split shipping/receiving.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Extensive trailer-parking rows at the NE corner of the property, plus trailers staged along the SE dock apron; many parked without tractors.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Dedicated trailer-storage rows fill the NE corner lot, distinct from active dock staging.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Very deep paved dock yard on the SE side gives generous interior queueing room ahead of the doors.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Aurora / Gateway Park, Denver metro. A residential subdivision abuts the site directly to the north and other large warehouses surround it — dense developed metro fabric, classified Urban.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: One large warehouse (~535,000 sq ft Gateway Park DC). The smaller buildings to the south are separate tenants, not part of this site.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Truck driveways are uncontrolled; lane counts are nominal single-lane drive widths.

citations.claim: UNFI's FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 2 Properties, lists a distribution centre at "Aurora, Colorado" as of 2025-08-02. Our roster address for this record is "17901 E 40th Ave, Aurora, CO 80011".

divestitureCheck.method: Checked against UNFI's FY2025 10-K property table and against its publicly announced 2025-2026 network consolidation. UNFI has closed 12 distribution centres in six years, so presence on the 10-K list alone is not treated as proof of current operation; the announced closures were checked by name.
divestitureCheck.result: present on the FY2025 property list and not named in any announced closure

sources.covers: UNFI network optimisation, the Allentown PA closure, and Central-region consolidations

verification.claimScope: CITY-LEVEL identity only. The 10-K names the city, not the parcel. This record is `probable` rather than `confirmed` because no retrieved source ties UNFI to the specific parcel traced here.
verification.rationale: PROBABLE: UNFI's own SEC 10-K property table lists a distribution centre in Aurora, Colorado as of 2025-08-02, and this record sits in that city. That establishes the company operates a DC there. It does NOT establish that the parcel traced here is that DC, and no source retrieved in this pass closes that gap, so the verdict stops at probable.
